messages:
eli_devex: Heads-up 1: support ticket where `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main` fails on macOS/arm with:
```
ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects
```
User is on Python 3.11.

 tori_engineer: thanks. Historically that's either a PEP 517 backend problem (poetry-core vs setuptools) or pip on the user machine is old and can't build from poetry-core sdists. Also if no wheel exists for arm, pip will fall back to sdist and try to compile native deps.

sam_pkg: confirmed pyproject currently uses `poetry-core` as build-backend. Two related issues I spotted: 1) we didn't include `redwood/py.typed` in the package so type consumers get nothing; 2) our `__init__.py` doesn't re-export AsyncClient so `from redwood import AsyncClient` fails when installed from wheel (editable installs mask that).

build-bot: CI packaging job failed for PR #1499: macos-arm64 wheel build error. Log: https://ci.internal/logs/1499

eli_devex: can we give the user a short workaround while we fix packaging?

kai_support: suggested workaround I already sent: upgrade pip/tooling then build + install wheel locally:
```
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build
python -m build
pip install dist/redwood-*.whl
```
For poetry users: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt && pip install -r reqs.txt`. Worked in tests.

tori_engineer: minimal code changes to unblock: 1) add `redwood/py.typed` to package include (MANIFEST.in or pyproject include), 2) export AsyncClient in `redwood/__init__.py` (`from .async_client import AsyncClient` and add to __all__), 3) optionally change `pyproject.build-system` to `setuptools`+`wheel` for better VCS/pip compatibility or at least document pip>=23 requirement.

sam_pkg: I'll open a tiny PR that adds MANIFEST.in entry, the export in __init__, and a packaging smoke test in CI. Test will create a clean venv, `pip install dist/*.whl`, then `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient; import pkgutil; print(bool(pkgutil.get_data('redwood','py.typed')))"` to assert both import and py.typed presence.

eli_devex: long-term we should add cibuildwheel to produce manylinux and macOS universal2 wheels so users on arm don't need to compile locally. That will also reduce onboarding friction for new teams.

kai_support: I've drafted a KB article with repro steps, the CLI workaround above, and a note about lockfile vs VCS installs: poetry.lock is ignored by `pip install git+...` so users should use `poetry export` if they need the lock constraints. I'll link it in the ticket.

tori_engineer: one more gotcha: some consumers pin transitive native deps in poetry.lock which leads to different resolver behavior when installing from pypi vs installing from source. Good to call that out in docs.

sam_pkg: PR #1499 created with packaging fixes + smoke test. Requesting CI run.

build-bot: Rerun requested for PR #1499.

eli_devex: thanks folks. Once CI passes can we publish a patch wheel and ping the affected users with the shorter install path? I'll mark the ticket waiting on release. :rocket:
